messages:
alex.k: heads-up — got a customer escal for high latency on /v1/generate. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 to ~3.8s over the last 10m. customer: widget-inc, affected region: us-east-1. I can share request IDs if needed.
alertbot: ALERT: latency-p99-high /v1/generate — 3.8s (threshold: 1.5s) — fired 1763002460 — links: <https://alerts.internal/latency/1763002460>
maria_s: on it. quick triage: which model variant is serving that route? any recent deploys to production in that window?
samir-ops: looks like model=redwood-xl-qa @ us-east-1a. last deploy was 1763001000 (small config tweak to batching). I don't see a failed deploy event in deploy-bot logs but will double-check.
deploy-bot: Release 2025.03.14-3 applied to canaries at 1763000955 and to prod at 1763001000 — change: default batch_size increased from 8 -> 12 for route /v1/generate.
alex.k: hmm batch size bump lines up with regression. but the p99 jump seems bigger than batching alone. any saturation on the host GPUs? logs show long GC-like stalls in runtime.
maria_s: pulling metrics (prom queries):
```
max_over_time(node_gpu_mem_utilization{region="us-east-1"}[15m]) --> 92%
sum(rate(redwood_inference_request_count{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (model) --> spike to 420r/s
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le)) --> 3.8
```
samir-ops: immediate mitigations we should try (in order):
- enforce stricter per-API-key rate limits for noisy customers (apply for widget-inc and any other heavy keys).
- enable circuit breaker on route to start failing fast for long tails and give runtime time to recover.
- add fallback routing to a lower-cost / lower-latency model variant or alternate region (us-west-2) while we investigate.
- revert the batch_size change if it correlates.

quick CLI snippets to apply the mitigation now:
```
# set per-key rate limit
redwood admin rate-limits create --api-key pk_widget_inc --route /v1/generate --limit 60 --window 1s

# enable circuit breaker to trip at 20% error/latency budget
redwood admin route update --route /v1/generate --circuit-breaker-threshold 0.20 --circuit-breaker-window 30s

# add fallback routing policy
redwood admin route update --route /v1/generate --fallback '[[{"type":"model","name":"redwood-medium-1"},{"type":"region","name":"us-west-2"}]]'
```
alex.k: I'm applying the rate limit to the offending key and enabling a fallback to redwood-medium-1 in us-west-2. will watch metrics now.
jess_product: please include customer comms. widget-inc is on high-visibility contract. we should tell them we're applying mitigations and will follow up with RCA.
samir-ops: status update 3m after mitigations:
```
p95 before: 1.2s -> after: 310ms
p99 before: 3.8s -> after: 720ms
request rate for /v1/generate dropped from 420r/s -> ~180r/s (because of rate-limits + fallback)
```
samir-ops: Prom query I used:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
maria_s: good progress. next steps:
- keep rate-limits and fallback in place for 1h while we complete root-cause.
- rollback the batch_size bump in a controlled canary if we still see tail after fallback removed.
- capture runtime logs and GPU metrics for the pre/post windows and attach to the incident ticket.

jess_product: long-term guardrails we need to add to avoid this class of regressions:
- enforce automated canary SLO checks for p95/p99 on any batching/serving-change before full rollout.
- synthetic tests that exercise tail latency at scale (not just avg).
- automatic circuit-breaker + fallback policies that trigger on p99 breach (configurable by product tier).
- per-customer adaptive rate-limits: high-traffic keys get progressive throttling rather than full throttles.

proposal for SLOs and automated actions (to review):
- SLOs: p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms for /v1/generate (gold tier).
- If p99 > 1.5s for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> trigger circuit breaker and route 50% traffic to fallback.
- If p99 > 3s -> escalate to SEV and throttle top 10% noisy API keys automatically.

samir-ops: added a quick routing policy (applied):
```
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "slo": {"p95":"0.3s","p99":"0.8s"},
  "automations": [
    {"trigger":"p99>1.5s@2m","action":"enable_circuit_breaker","params":{"trip_rate":0.2}},
    {"trigger":"p99>3s@1m","action":"throttle_top_keys","params":{"percentile":"90","limit":"30r/s"}}
  ]
}
```
alex.k: filing postmortem ticket PRE-1763002468 and adding runbook checklist. assign to @samir-ops for RCA and @maria_s for metric dashboards updates. I'll draft the customer note and loop in account team.
deploy-bot: Rollback request queued: revert batch_size change on /v1/generate to 8 (canary 10m -> full if green) — runbook approval required.

maria_s: note for follow-up: investigate why batch_size increase caused tail — might be interaction with KV cache and GPU kernel selection (compilation paths). also audit the canary SLO test suite; it missed this because p99 not covered.
jess_product: thanks team. once RCA is in ticket we can publish a short summary to the customer and update the public docs for SLO guardrails.

alex.k: closing here — mitigation held, metrics stable for 12m. leaving open until postmortem and canary test updates done. :thumbsup:
